interfaces_and_contracts:
The README.md section will document these concrete interfaces and contracts:
- Generic event guard: POST /rooms/:roomId/events checks requiresGovernedPath and refuses task.dispatched.planner (T2), plan.submitted (T3), plan.revision_requested (T4), plan.approved (T5), and founder.cancel (T22) with 403 governed_path_required before the ledger.
- Founder goal on T1: prepareFounderGoal accepts an optional non-empty goal (up to 20,000 chars, scanned by containsCredentialMaterial) on scope.captured (T1) only, refuses caller-supplied founder_goal evidence (400 founder_goal_refused), and appends evidence { kind: 'founder_goal', ref: event.eventId, digest: founderGoalDigest(goal) }.
- Deterministic command IDs: plannerCommandIdFor(roomId, openingEventId, attempt = 1) hashes build-room/planner-command/v1\0${roomId}\0${openingEventId} (adding \0attempt-${attempt} for attempts 2..MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS, where MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS is 3) with SHA-256 to produce cmd_planner_<32 hex>.
- Plan read route: GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan (planReadRouter, behind CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN) finds the room's latest T3 entry without a room-state check, loads the plan from PlanStore.planForEvent (re-judged with plan_hash recomputed), re-reads the room to ensure no newer T3 landed (409 plan_changed if superseded), and answers 200 { roomId, commandId, planHash, document } or 404 room_not_found / plan_not_found.
- Plan decision route: POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision (planDecisionRouter, behind PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN and requireLeader; 503 plan_decision_disabled when unset) records plan.approved (T5), plan.revision_requested (T4), or founder.cancel (T22) atomically with its journal decision row (authorizationRef founder-credential/PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN) via journal.inTransaction(client).appendDecision. For founder.cancel, a room with no journaled planner command answers 409 founder_cancel_unavailable; if any command is pending, the cancel commits as an unconfirmed cancel (unconfirmedCancelRecorded: true) and appends an unresolved command row for each pending command in the same transaction.
- Counted-run routes: countedRunRouter mounts POST and GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/planner-round and GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal behind PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN (503 counted_run_disabled when unset) and PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN parsed by parseCountedRunConfig (503 counted_run_not_configured when unset).
- Gateway pull channel: POST /gateway/planner/poll (16 KB limit) and POST /gateway/planner/report (256 KB limit) carry signed planner requests (attest, execute, status) and reports.
- Antigravity executor: AgyPlannerExecutor runs on Linux on Gateway 1880c12d-d98d-4a91-b25a-23320aa7f58a when BUILDROOM_PLANNER_EXECUTOR is agy and BUILDROOM_PLANNER_USER, BUILDROOM_PLANNER_AGY, BUILDROOM_PLANNER_AGY_SHA256, and BUILDROOM_PLANNER_CHECKOUTS are set, invoking sudo -n -u <planner user> -- <agyPath> with PINNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS (--input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --model gemini-4-argon-high --effort high --mode plan --sandbox --print-timeout 900s).
data_flow:
The README.md section will trace one planning round end to end:
1. Scope capture (T1): The Founder posts scope.captured with goal; prepareFounderGoal attaches the server-computed founder_goal evidence entry (ref set to event.eventId).
2. Opening the round: In PlannerLoop.runRound(roomId), from SCOPED, openFirstRound uses ledger.appendDerived to commit T2 (task.dispatched.planner, with gatewayOnline derived by the fence and rolesAssigned / reviewerIsNotBuilder derived from roomRoles) and journal.inTransaction(client).appendJournaled in one transaction. From PLANNING after T4 (or after a prior attempt failed as not_sent within retryBudgetTransition up to MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS = 3), openNextAttempt uses ledger.underRoomLock to journal the next command bound to the opening T2 or T4 event.
3. Pre-contact checks and dispatch: Before contacting a provider, executeRound checks route coverage via authorizeRoute and calls planner.attest(commandId), verifying that the returned ExecutionIdentity has role architect and matches the intended provider, model, and executionSurface, then appends identity_bound. It then calls planner.dispatch(work). On the Antigravity lane, AgyPlannerExecutor checks that no planner-user process is running, verifies the SHA-256 of agyPath, creates a read-only shallow git checkout at baseSha, starts agy under sudo with PINNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS, waits for the first stream-json event to be init with init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high' and a non-empty conversation_id, writes the durable EvidenceRecord (commandId, executionId, startedAt, agySha256, initModel, conversationId, sent, endedAt, outcome, exitCode, signal, checkoutRemoved) with sent: true, and only then writes the prompt to agy's stdin. The loop requires PlannerInit on the antigravity/google lane and appends dispatched (encoded as BRJ:c:2 with initModel and providerConversationId).
4. Plan judgement and T3 submission: When agy finishes, it reaps the planner user with sudo -n -u <planner user> -- /usr/bin/pkill -KILL -u <planner user>, checks remainsAfterReap, removes the checkout, and writes the closing EvidenceRecord. The loop receives the document via planner.awaitPlan(commandId), validates it with judgeRoundPlan (PLANDOC_SCHEMA_V1, PLAN_READY_FOR_FOUNDER_APPROVAL, canonical scope_paths within captured scope, matching repository and base_sha), and calls submitRoundPlan to commit T3 (plan.submitted), plans.inTransaction(client).recordPlan, and journal.inTransaction(client).appendCommandEvent (completed, checked by the journal's completion authorization resolver) in one transaction.
5. Founder read and decision: The Founder reads the plan via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan and submits T5, T4, or T22 via POST /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan-decision.
trust_and_security_boundaries:
The README.md section will highlight four trust boundaries enforced by the implementation:
1. Three distinct bearer tokens in packages/control-plane/src/config.ts (each at least 32 characters of the RFC 6750 alphabet and pairwise distinct): CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN (room routes, journal append, plan read), PHASE3_ADJUDICATION_TOKEN (plan-decision route only), and PHASE4_COUNTED_RUN_TOKEN (counted-run planner-round and journal routes only).
2. Server-derived guard facts and single-transaction atomicity: callers cannot post T2, T3, T4, T5, or T22 to POST /rooms/:roomId/events; guard facts for G2, G3, G4, G5, and G22 are computed by the control plane under the leadership fence and room lock; T2+journaled, T3+plan+completed, and T4/T5/T22+decision each commit in a single Postgres transaction under br_app_runtime.
3. Credential redaction and refusal: containsCredentialMaterial guards T1 goals, journal rows, stored plans in build_room_plans, plan-decision inputs, and Phase 4 counted-run evidence files; logPlanRefused logs only schema-declared paths, array indices, violation codes, and bounds without echoing untrusted plan text.
4. Gateway host isolation: AgyPlannerExecutor runs only on Linux on Gateway 1880c12d-d98d-4a91-b25a-23320aa7f58a, executes the root-owned hash-verified agy binary as the unprivileged planner user with PINNED_AGY_ARGUMENTS in plan mode over a read-only anonymous checkout, holds back the prompt until init.model === 'gemini-4-argon-high' and conversation_id are verified, reaps all planner-user processes after every run and at boot, and latches planner-halted.json on any cleanup, reap, checkout-removal, or evidence failure.
migration_and_compatibility: The canonical migration sequence in packages/control-plane/src/migrations.ts runs from 0001_ledger_core through 0010_plan_store (10 migrations total). Phase 4 adds migration 0010_plan_store, which creates the append-only table public.build_room_plans keyed by command_id with a unique constraint and foreign key on (room_id, lifecycle_event_id) referencing public.build_room_events, a statement-level immutability trigger rejecting UPDATE, DELETE, and TRUNCATE, and SELECT, INSERT grants to br_app_runtime. Command-event row format BRJ:c:2 (SPEC_ID_C2) required no database migration because command_journal_events stores canonical row_bytes opaque to SQL. Because this plan modifies only README.md, it has zero runtime or schema compatibility impact.
error_and_failure_behavior:
The README.md section will summarize the fail-closed refusal and recovery behavior:
- Pre-send vs unknown-contact failures: Attempts that provably never contacted a provider (such as authorization failure, attestation failure, identity mismatch, or agy refusing before stdin is written) record failed; only not_sent failures may be retried within the round's retryBudgetTransition budget (up to MAX_ROUND_ATTEMPTS = 3). Any dispatch or wait error where contact cannot be ruled out records unresolved and blocks further retries.
- Plan refusals: Invalid, non-ready, or out-of-scope plans record failed (plan_invalid or plan_outside_captured_scope), emit a structured planner.plan_refused log entry with no plan text, and never write to build_room_plans.
- Recovery: PlannerRecovery.recoverRoom(roomId) verifies the journal chain from genesis via journal.verify() and queries planner.reconcile(commandId) to reconcile an open journaled, identity_bound, dispatched, or unresolved command without re-dispatching. Nothing in the service calls recoverRoom at startup; only tests invoke it.
- Gateway halt latch: If agy exit is unconfirmed, a planner-user process survives pkill, a checkout cannot be removed, or an evidence file cannot be written or read, AgyPlannerExecutor writes planner-halted.json and refuses further planner work until the Founder removes the marker.
observability:
Observability across the Phase 4 loop consists of:
1. The hash-chained Postgres command journal (command_journal_events, verified from genesis by JournalStore.verify and readable per room via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/journal) and the append-only plan store (build_room_plans, readable for the latest T3 via GET /control-plane/rooms/:roomId/plan).
2. Structured JSON console logs for planner.plan_refused (carrying roomId, commandId, classification, and sanitized PlanRefusalReason) and Gateway executor events (including agy.not_sent and agy.halted).
3. Per-command durable worker records in <gatewayDirectory>/planner/ and supplemental executor EvidenceRecord files in <gatewayDirectory>/planner-evidence/ (holding commandId, executionId, startedAt, agySha256, initModel, conversationId, sent, endedAt, outcome, exitCode, signal, checkoutRemoved, and closing diagnostics streamEvents, resultStatus, responseBytes, invalidEscapesRepaired, answersJoined).
